summary.headline: Bikaji Q2 FY27 top line grew close to 13% as Diwali shifted to Q3; management guides FY27 growth to about 17% and Q4 EBITDA to 13.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew close to 13% in Q2 FY27, but the quarter was distorted by Diwali and sweets/gifting shifting into Q3 (October). Snacking carried the quarter, with value growth of about 22% and volume growth of about 15%, while total volume growth was about 5%. Gross margin was 34.4% in Q2, with standalone gross margin hit by about 1.7% from raw material inflation (pulses, edible oil, packaging, diesel), and consolidated EBITDA was about 12.6% in H1. Management says a roughly 3% MRP price increase takes effect from around 15 November, with full price impact in Q4, and expects Q3 to be margin-pressured and Q4 to normalise.

financial_highlights.change: standalone gross margin hit about 1.7%; about 2% vs Q1 standalone per Q&A, 0.6% consolidated

financial_highlights.value: 0.7% increase in ad cost as % of sales vs last year (standalone)

financial_highlights.metric: Packaged sweets share of total business

segments.name: Snacking (Ethnic and Western)
segments.commentary: Snacking grew about 20%+ in core markets and about 35%+ in focus markets; Western Snacks grew 44% and Ethnic Snacks 19.7% in Q2. Impulse INR 5 and INR 10 packs grew about 20%.

segments.name: Packaged Sweets and Gifting
segments.commentary: Sweets and gifting were weak in Q2 as festive demand moved into Q3; management expects Q2+Q3 combined sweets growth above 10% YTD December. Sweets are about 12.5% of total business, about 25% in focus states.

segments.name: THF (The Handmade Factory / premium sweets and retail)
segments.commentary: FY27 THF revenue guided at INR 160-170 crore (60-70% growth) with stores rising from about 34 to 31-33 by year end (other statement says 40); same-store growth 6-8% in the first six months.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Focus markets grew 7.6% in Q2 and core markets 17.5%; other states declined, as sweets concentration is highest there.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company revenue growth guided at high-teens, about 17%; YTD Q2+Q3 growth target raised to 17% plus from 15% plus.
Second-half growth expected at high-teens to about 20%+; focus-market growth expected at 20-23% in H2.
Q3 margins expected under pressure as price increase only takes effect from about 15 November; Q4 gross margin and EBITDA expected to normalise, with Q4 EBITDA about 13.5% and exit run rate of 13%+.
About 3% MRP price increase from around 15 November; management sees no further major price increase until March 2027 unless conditions change.
Commodity relief expected: edible oil and packaging prices softening, diesel down, pulses expected to ease after new crop in December.
A&P spend held at about 2% of sales for FY27.
Paytm INR 5/10 cashback offer runs September to March; Bikaji says no cash payout to Paytm, cost is packaging change and collateral.
capex_capacity: Retail store network about 34 stores, expected to reach 40 by year end per one remark; later remark cites 31-33 stores at year end.
Bhujia production disrupted in Q1 by Bengal elections; new mother depot set up to hold extra inventory against future disruptions.
Bikaneri Bhujia GI tag applies only to output made in Bikaner; alternate-location production will be labelled as besan bhujia, not Bikaneri Bhujia.
THF experimenting with 600-800 sq ft formats alongside 2,000-2,500 sq ft stores; premium Foundré by THF store in Gurgaon due next month.
Added about 20,000 outlets in Q2; company says it will overdeliver its annual distribution target.
demand_pricing: October demand was strong across general trade, modern trade and all channels; management indicated October YoY growth could be around 50%, driven by sweets shift.
Market share commentary: competition is strong but focus-state growth was not impacted, per management; Q2 decline attributed to sweets timing.
Price hikes not taken in Sept-Oct due to festive gift-box lead times; post-Diwali MRP increase is about 3% (3-3.5% per later remark).
Grammage cut of about 3-4% (weighted average) on INR 5 and INR 10 small packs.
Dal and pulse prices rose sharply (dal moth about INR 85-90 to about INR 135 per management's cited example).

qa_highlights.question: Is the focus market slowdown only due to sweets shifting to Q3 or also competition from Haldiram, Balaji and regional players? What share of sweets comes from focus markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says focus states outperformed and the slowdown is solely due to gifting/sweets timing; sweets are about 12.5% of total business and about 25% in focus states.

qa_highlights.question: What growth to expect in H2 for company and focus markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus markets 20-23%; company high-teens to about 20% in H2 and about 17% for full year.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q3 margins improve on mix and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 will be under pressure as price increases take effect only from about 15 November, with about 40 days of benefit in Q3; Q4 will normalise, with exit run rate EBITDA 13%+.

qa_highlights.question: Did out-of-home consumption get hit by the heat wave?
qa_highlights.answer: No material impact seen; INR 5 and INR 10 single-serve and Western Snacks (mostly on-the-go) grew well.

qa_highlights.question: Is competition intensifying given sharp FMCG price hikes elsewhere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says food and home care are not comparable; price hikes were held back for festive gift-box timing, and the post-Diwali increase is industry-wide.

qa_highlights.question: Progress on alternate Bhujia manufacturing locations and GI tag impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhujia growth is about 20% post Q1 disruption; a mother depot added for buffer stock; alternate-location output cannot carry the Bikaneri Bhujia name.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 30%, and what is full-year margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone gross margin hit about 2% vs last quarter, consolidated 0.6%, from input costs; ad spend up 0.7% of sales; H1 EBITDA about 12.6-13%, Q4 about 13.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected THF full-year revenue and store trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: THF FY27 revenue INR 160-170 crore (60-70% growth) vs about INR 100 crore last year; same-store growth 6-8%; 31-33 stores by year end.

risks_watch: Q3 gross margin and EBITDA pressure until the 3% price hike is realised from about 15 November; the full benefit only shows in Q4.
Pulse and edible oil inflation; management's 'no further price increase until March' depends on commodities easing as expected.
Sweets and gifting timing: Q2 and Q3 must be read together, so Q3 must show the catch-up for the 17% YTD target.
Paytm cashback scheme runs to March, with unclear impact on realisations and packaging change costs.
Bikaner production disruption risk and GI tag limits on output made outside Bikaner.
Inconsistency in store-count guidance (40 vs 31-33 by year end) and THF margin contribution needs clarification.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and snacking momentum, with specific numeric guidance for H2 and Q4. More cautious on Q3 margins and input costs, and some answers were vague on store counts and the post-Diwali price move.
key_quotes: Our top line growth is close to 13% in quarter 2.
We are looking at 17% plus growth at YTD level.
Quarter 4 will be normalized gross margin and EBITDA.
I think we will not require any further price increase till March end, unless something different happens.

adds.what: THF retail stores (premium sweets) rising from about 34 to 31-33 by year end per later remark (one remark said 40)
Mother depot set up to hold extra Bhujia inventory against future disruptions

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth to about 17% (high teens) and THF revenue to INR 160-170 crore (60-70%), with H2 growth at high-teens to 20%+, backed mainly by a ~3% MRP hike from mid-November, snacking volume growth of ~15%, and commodity relief, though no specific capacity additions or order book numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA guided at about 13.5% with exit run-rate 13%+, as the ~3% MRP hike from about 15 November (about 40 days of benefit in Q3) and commodity relief (edible oil, packaging, diesel softening; pulses easing after December crop) normalise margins, though Q2 standalone gross margin fell about 1.7-2% on input inflation and Q3 is guided to be under pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Retail store network is about 34 stores, with management giving 31-33 by year end (one remark said 40), and THF is trialling 600-800 sq ft formats; no plant or line capacity addition was announced, and the mother depot is a buffer, not capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Snacking volume grew about 15% in Q2 and H2 company growth is guided at high-teens to about 20%+ (focus markets 20-23%), though total volume growth was only about 5% in Q2 and sweets growth is guided only upwards of 10% for Q2+Q3 combined.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex figure or utilisation level was disclosed and no new plant was discussed; the THF store rollout and the Bhujia alternate-location setup are the only expansion items mentioned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth was raised to about 17% (YTD Q2+Q3 target raised to 17%+ from 15%+) and October demand was strong with a possible ~50% YoY, but Q3 margin pressure and input costs limit upside to the margin guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 gross margin and EBITDA are guided under pressure until the price hike takes effect around 15 November, and the Q2+Q3 sweets growth target was cut to upwards of 10%, so a Q3 miss is a real risk if pulses and edible oil stay high.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Premium Foundré by THF store in Gurgaon is due next month (about Dec 2026), and THF is experimenting with 600-800 sq ft formats, but no new product SKUs with size or revenue were named.

rows.label: ~3% MRP hike from ~15 Nov 2026, no further major hike until March 2027
rows.why: Price increase is set to take effect around 15 November with about 40 days of benefit in Q3 and full impact in Q4, while management sees no further major increase until March 2027 unless conditions change, so Q4 price realisation is locked in.

rows.label: THF retail expansion and FY27 revenue INR 160-170 Cr
rows.why: THF FY27 revenue is guided at INR 160-170 crore (60-70% growth on about INR 100 crore) with same-store growth of 6-8% and retail contribution up 58% in Q2 and 64% YTD, though store count guidance conflicts (31-33 vs 40).

rows.label: Commodity relief and A&P held at ~2% of sales
rows.why: Edible oil and packaging are softening, diesel is down, and pulses are expected to ease after the December new crop, while A&P is held at about 2% of sales for FY27, supporting the Q4 margin recovery to about 13.5%.
